summary: 1933 80-ft steel tower on Fox Butte, Deschutes NF; 1926 fire damage disputed; unmanned, gated road; 2021 removal proposal listed as cancelled.

facts.design: 80-ft steel Aermotor tower with metal 7 by 7 ft cab; gable-roof L-4 ground cabin moved from Sixteen Butte in 1948

access.note: A locked gate on the access road is about three-quarters of a mile below the summit; visitors walk the rest. No source says the tower is open to climbing.

visit.trail_note: Walk past the locked gate; a 2021 visitor walked 1.1 miles to the summit. The cabin is in disrepair and the tower's first landing is the highest point that visitor reached. Do not climb.

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Deschutes National Forest

events.note: Heliograph set up on the west point; lookout Oscar Harding posted at the station
Telephone line built from the Cabin Lake Ranger Station to the west point
Standard D-6 cupola constructed on the west point
Fire swept the summit in August 1926; sources disagree on whether the cupola or the tower burned
March 1927 preliminary budget draft allotted $250 for a new Fox Butte lookout station
80-ft steel Aermotor tower with 7x7 cab completed in June 1933; cabin from the west point moved to the tower site
Gable-roof L-4 cabin moved from Sixteen Butte to replace the earlier ground cabin
Station abandoned overnight in July 1959 as a fire burned around it
Staffed full time while the East Butte lookout was rebuilt; duties returned in 1996
Forest Service building disposal project proposed removing the tower and cabin; project summary now lists it as cancelled

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The L-4 in the record is the ground cabin moved from Sixteen Butte in 1948; the lookout itself is the 80-ft steel Aermotor tower with a metal 7x7 cab.

corrections.proposed: 80-ft steel Aermotor tower with 7x7 metal cab; L-4 ground cabin from Sixteen Butte (1948)
corrections.why: The register and firelookout.com describe an 80-ft steel tower; the L-4 is the ground cabin, not the tower

notes_for_editor: Disputed 1926 damage: the register says the cupola burned, Bend newspapers of August 1926 say the lookout tower was destroyed, and a January 1927 report says the tower was not burned but two supports were. The story says the sources disagree. Elevation: the register gives 6,065 ft (the record's 1848.6 m); firelookout.com and the 2021 directory give 6,025 ft. Record matches the register; not changed. Current status: the 2021 visitor wrote that the Forest Service proposed removal; the FS project page (last updated Feb 2025) lists it cancelled, so the removal threat may be over but no current agency statement was found. Access: gated road, not a public visit; the story recommends not climbing. Newspaper transcriptions are on the weebly page and were not checked against original newspaper scans.
